class.name: SchemaCore
class.brief_description: The ordered, typed column list two peers must agree on, and nothing else.
class.description: A schema is declaration and no storage. It exists once so the row-major property binding, the column-major table binding, and the database read the same column list instead of three that drift, which is what makes [method compute_hash] a real skew check rather than a check of one binding against itself. [codeblock] declare consume ──────────────────────────── ──────────────────────────────────────── declare(schema, name) column_key / column_type / column_stride add_column(schema, key, ...) hash_of(schema) the shape, wire-visible set_column_quantizer(...) find(name) seal(schema) fixes order [/codeblock] Declaration order is the address order, so a column's index is what every binding addresses it by. [method seal] is what fixes that order: a schema that could still gain a column has no stable address to hand out and no hash worth comparing. [br][br]Re-declaring a sealed schema is idempotent rather than an error, because a script reload re-runs every declaration it owns. The replay walks a cursor through the sealed columns and a genuine shape change fails at [method seal] instead of silently shifting every index. [br][br]The verbs come in two halves. The [RID]-keyed half is what a session calls, and the [SchemaRecord]-facing half ([method append_column], [method assign_quantizer], [method fix]) is what a declaration with no session to key it uses.

method.name: add_column
method.description: Appends one column in address order and returns its index, or [code]-1[/code]. [br][br]Against a sealed record this is the idempotent re-declaration path: the column must match the one already sitting at the re-declaration cursor, which is what makes a script reload replay its own schema and a changed schema fail loudly instead of silently shifting every index.

method.name: append_column
method.description: Appends one column to [param record] and returns its index, the record-facing half of [method add_column]. [br][br]Refuses an empty [param key], a [param stride] below one, a [param type] outside [enum ColumnType], and a key the record already holds.

method.name: assign_quantizer
method.description: Assigns one column's quantizer on [param record], the record-facing half of [method set_column_quantizer]. Does nothing once the record is sealed.

method.name: column_at
method.description: Returns [param record]'s column at [param column], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: column_count
method.description: Returns how many columns [param schema] declares.

method.name: column_key
method.description: Returns one column's key, or an empty name when the address is invalid.

method.name: column_quantizer
method.description: Returns one column's quantizer, or [code]null[/code] for the memcpy path.

method.name: column_stride
method.description: Returns how many elements one row occupies in [param column], or [code]0[/code] when the address is invalid.

method.name: column_type
method.description: Returns one column's [enum ColumnType], or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: compute_hash
method.description: Folds the name and every column's visible shape into the u16 a table frame header carries and a property set's wire hash is built on. [br][br]The quantizer is part of the shape because two peers that packed the same column to different bit widths cannot read each other. The formula is the contract, not the implementation: changing it changes the bytes on the wire.

method.name: declare
method.description: Opens a declaration for [param schema] under [param name]. [br][br]Records the schema on first call and restarts the re-declaration cursor on every later one, so a script reload replays its columns through [method add_column] against the record it already sealed. [br][br]A schema with no columns is legal and meaningful: as a table it is a tag, and its commits carry membership alone.

method.name: element_type
method.description: Returns the [enum Variant.Type] one element of [param type] reads as, which is the type a [NetwQuantize] is asked to support and encode, or [code]-1[/code] outside [enum ColumnType]. [br][br][constant VARIANT] reads as [constant @GlobalScope.TYPE_NIL], because a self-describing element has no one type to pack.

method.name: find
method.description: Returns the schema declared under [param name], or an invalid [RID].

method.name: find_column
method.description: Returns the index of the column named [param key], or [code]-1[/code]. [br][br]The name lookup exists because a caller who knows a property by name needs the one address it has, and a linear walk over a handful of columns is cheaper than a second index that could disagree.

method.name: fix
method.description: Fixes [param record] and its shape hash, the record-facing half of [method seal].

method.name: has_stride
method.description: Returns whether [param schema] declares any column of stride greater than one, the question a binding with no stride vocabulary must ask.

method.name: has_variant
method.description: Returns whether [param schema] declares any [constant VARIANT] column, the one question a fixed-width binding must ask before it compiles.

method.name: hash_of
method.description: Returns [param schema]'s sealed shape hash, or [code]0[/code] when it is not sealed. [br][br]The shape is the name and, per column, key, type, stride, and quantizer. It is what a table frame carries and what a property set folds its membership into, so two peers that declared a different type or packed a column to a different bit width disagree here rather than misreading every later frame.

method.name: is_valid
method.description: Returns whether [param schema] names a declared record.

method.name: make_storage
method.description: Returns an empty storage array for [param type], the shape a table's writes and its decoder both fill. Returns [code]null[/code] for a type outside [enum ColumnType].

method.name: name_of
method.description: Returns [param schema]'s declared name, or an empty name.

method.name: open_redeclare
method.description: Restarts [param record]'s re-declaration cursor, the record-facing half of [method declare].

method.name: quantizer_tag
method.description: Returns the shape tag [method compute_hash] folds for one column's quantizer, the class name and bit width or [code]"raw"[/code].

method.name: record_of
method.description: Returns the [SchemaRecord] [param schema] names, or [code]null[/code]. [br][br]The one door between the [RID]-keyed half and the record-facing half. A binding that must hold a declaration rather than query it, such as [method TableCore.declare], takes it from here.

method.name: seal
method.description: Fixes [param schema]'s declaration and its shape hash. [br][br]Sealing is what makes declaration order address order, so a record that could still gain a column could not be read by a binding that sealed earlier. Re-sealing a record whose re-declaration replayed fewer columns than it holds is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED], because the two declarations disagree.

method.name: set_column_quantizer
method.description: Assigns [param quantizer] to one column before sealing. [br][br]A column with no quantizer takes the raw little-endian memcpy path, which is the fastest thing a table does and the widest thing it sends.

method.name: storage_type
method.description: Returns the [enum Variant.Type] of the storage array [param type] compiles to, or [code]-1[/code] outside [enum ColumnType]. [br][br]Wire width is a separate concern, which is why the narrow integers share one storage type.

method.name: type_from_variant
method.description: Returns the [enum ColumnType] a property of [param variant_type] compiles to, [constant VARIANT] for anything the fixed-width tier cannot name. [br][br]The narrow integers are never inferred, because reflection cannot know a range. They stay hand-declared table vocabulary.

constants.constant: [PackedFloat64Array]. 64 bits on the wire. Present because GDScript floats are 64 bit, so forcing an accumulator through [constant F32] would be an opinion about the caller's precision.
[PackedVector4Array] read as [Quaternion], distinct from [constant VECTOR4] because smallest-three quantization ([NetwQuantizeQuaternion]) is a semantic rather than a width.
[PackedInt64Array] of routes, encoded as varints because routes are small. Resolve one back to a handle with [method NetwMultiplayer.rid_from_route].

[Array]. The self-describing tier, variable width on the wire, which is what a [String] or a [Dictionary] property compiles to. Refused by [method TableCore.declare], because variable width has no memcpy and no row budget.
